entities.summary: Geoffrey Gurrumul Yunupingu, commonly known as Gurrumul and also referred to since his death as Dr G. Yunupingu, was a Yolŋu Aboriginal Australian musician. A multi-instrumentalist, he played drums, keyboards, guitar and didgeridoo, but is best known for the clarity of his singing voice. He sang stories of his land both in Yolŋu languages, such as Gaalpu, Gumatj, or Djambarrpuynu, and in English. He began his career as a member of Yothu Yindi and later Saltwater Band, and his solo career brought him wider acclaim; he was the most commercially successful Aboriginal Australian musician at the time of his death.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a prominent Yolŋu Aboriginal Australian musician, Gurrumul's music played a significant role in promoting Indigenous Australian culture and language, with his songs reaching over 1 million people worldwide. His legacy continues to inspire new generations of artists and cultural leaders.
